messages:
alyssa: FYI noticed a throughput drop on the NF4 canary pool since the FP4/NF4 mix went live this morning. p95 token latency jumped ~2.3x on short seqs.
ben: omg, saw alerts. is this the KV memory spike we saw earlier?
acheng: can you share host ids / sample request ids?
alyssa: sample traces: host-gpu-12, host-gpu-14. request ids: f2a3c1, f2a3c2. short seqs ~32 tokens.
sre-jen: deploy-bot reports a kernel swap at 03:12 UTC: kernel-selector v2.4.1 -> v2.5.0 on pool A. commit 9f3a2b changed prefetch ordering.
ben: 9f3a2b was the change that reorders thin allocator to prefer slab-coalesced KV. suspect interaction with NF4 quant paths.
alyssa: attached flamegraph link: http://perf.internal/flame/2170032468 (shows heavy time in slowpath memcpy)
michael: telemetry dump shows repeated fallback to fallback_kernel_int8 for small seqs:
```
kernel_selector: select_kernel(model=nf4, seq=32) -> candidate=[fast_4bit_avx, fallback_int8] -> chosen=fallback_int8 (latency 9.2ms)
kv_cache: slab_alloc(size=512) -> returned=thin-alloc-idx=0xffffffff -> hostcopy
```
cheng: that hostcopy line is worrying — looks like thin allocator returned an out-of-band index and the runtime did host memcpy to satisfy KV miss.
ben: could be allocator fragmentation + new prefetch heuristics trying to pre-emptively fetch KV pages for NF4 but hitting underflow.
alyssa: repro command I ran locally:
```
# replay short sequence load
python tools/replay_load.py --model nf4-fp4-mix --clients 12 --seq-len 32 --requests 10000 --target-host host-gpu-12
```
I can repro ~20% throughput drop vs baseline.
sre-jen: opened a bisect job across kernel-selector commits. job id 2170032471.
ops-bot: bisect job 2170032471 started (expected ~45m).
michael: I grabbed a profiling trace with perf + nvprof on host-gpu-12, lines show repeated kernel context switches and memcpys between device-host-device which is confirmed by driver logs.
cheng: quick mitigation: revert prefetch ordering from 9f3a2b or disable thin-allocator coalescing flag. can we try a hotfix in canary?
ben: +1. try disabling thin-allocator coalesce via config: `runtime.kv.thin_coalesce=false` on pool A and roll.
alyssa: applying that now to pool A canary. will monitor.
(5m later)
alyssa: rollback config propagated. preliminary numbers: p95 down to ~1.1x baseline, throughput back to ~98% of previous. memory spikes reduced.
michael: confirms hostcopy events reduced in nvprof. good call.
cheng: bisect result so far: performance regression introduced by 9f3a2b when combined with `runtime.kv.prefetch=true` and short seq workload. standalone 9f3a2b without prefetch doesn't reproduce.
ben: suggests logic bug in combined path: prefetch triggers slab coalescing, which returns special thin token, but some kernel paths expect slab-aligned KV and call hostcopy on mismatch.
sre-jen: filing an engineering ticket with repro and trace: INF-7892. assign to @cheng and @michael.
cheng: will add a small guard in kernel-selector: verify slab token alignment before selecting coalesced path, fall back to conservative prefetched slab when mismatch.
michael: also we'll add telemetry counters: `kv.thin.alloc_failures`, `kernel.selected_via_coalesce`, `kv.hostcopy_events` to detect early.
alyssa: thanks. follow-up: we should run a short qa sweep across seq lengths [8,32,128,512] with nf4/fp4 mix to be safe. I can schedule.
ben: also let's mark this as a canary-only rollout hold until INF-7892 is resolved.
ops-bot: ticket INF-7892 created by sre-jen, priority=high, tags=[perf,quantization,kv,canary].
sre-jen: nice troubleshooting everyone. lessons: preftech + thin allocator + short seq = edgecase. add a unit test for slab-token invariants. :white_check_mark:
alyssa: agreed. I'll post a short postmortem once INF-7892 has a patch and we've validated across hosts. :pray:
